name: Magazine
summary: Consumer magazine print ads are supplied as CMYK press-ready PDFs at the publication's trim size plus bleed.
rules: Build full-page and spread files at trim plus 0.125in bleed per side; fractional ads usually take no bleed.
Supply a composite CMYK PDF (PDF/X-1a most commonly requested; X-4 only if the publication accepts it).
Embed all fonts and images; no RGB, spot or separated files unless the publication requests them.
Keep live matter 0.25in from trim; many publications ask 0.375-0.5in for full-bleed ads.
Trim size varies by title (8.5x11 is a common default, 7.875x10.5 also common); confirm with the rate card.

do: Place images at 300dpi at final size.
Use rich black for large solid areas and 100% K for small text.
Keep type and logos inside the safe area.
Flatten transparencies and outline or embed fonts via PDF/X export.
Request the publication's exact mechanical specs before building.
avoid: Running critical text or faces across the gutter fold.
Submitting RGB images or ICC-tagged RGB output.
Exceeding the ink limit with four-color black text.
Placing thin reversed type on a four-color background.
Relying on perfect left/right alignment across a spread.
tips: Spread crossovers can shift at binding; Afar advises 3/8in safety for critical crossovers.
Fractional ads may get a 0.30pt rule added by the publisher if edges are undefined.
Crop marks are typically offset 0.125-0.375in outside the bleed.
Check whether covers have different specs or require proofs.
Request a SWOP/GRACoL contract proof when color is critical.

sizes.label: Full Page
sizes.note: Trim size; add 0.125in bleed per side (8.75 x 11.25 file). Common default - confirm with the publication's rate card.

sizes.note: Typical non-bleed size on 8.5x11 trim; varies by title. Common default - confirm with the publication's rate card.

sizes.note: Typical non-bleed size on 8.5x11 trim; varies by title. Common default - confirm with the publication's rate card.

sizes.label: Two-Page Spread
sizes.note: Trim size; add 0.125in bleed (17.25 x 11.25 file). Keep critical type/imagery about 0.5in either side of the fold. Confirm with rate card.

sizes.label: Quarter Page
sizes.note: Typical non-bleed size on 8.5x11 trim; varies by title. Common default - confirm with the publication's rate card.

sizes.label: Digest Full Page
sizes.note: Digest-format trim (typical); add 0.125in bleed. Common default - confirm with the publication's rate card.

sizes.label: Full Page (7.875 x 10.5 trim)
sizes.note: Alternate common trim seen in Heat Treat Today and BetterInvesting specs; bleed file 8.125 x 10.75. Confirm with rate card.

confidence: Medium. Bleed/safety/PDF-X-1a/300dpi corroborated by several magazine spec pages; fractional-page sizes and the 8.5x11 trim are typical defaults, not sourced from one standard. 300% ink is conventional SWOP practice, not fetched from a primary source.

name: Newspaper
summary: Newspaper ads are sized in columns by inches (SAU) and supplied as PDF files, usually without bleed and often grayscale or ROP color.
colorProfile: Grayscale or newsprint CMYK (SNAP/Coated-No.5-style newsprint profile; confirm)
rules: Newspaper ads typically carry NO bleed; build to exact ad size (bleedIn 0).
Size ads to the publication's column grid: SAU column widths and depth in inches; widths vary by paper.
Supply PDF (PDF/X-1a or X-4 where requested) with fonts embedded; grayscale unless ROP color is booked.
Keep type about 0.25in inside the ad edge; border or rule keeps small ads clear of editorial.
Column widths below use the classic SAU basis (2-1/16in column, 1/8in gutter); many papers now run narrower webs - confirm.

do: Use 100% K for text and avoid four-color black on newsprint.
Use bold, high-contrast layouts and 9pt+ body type.
Add a thin border to ads with white backgrounds.
Request the paper's exact column widths and ad depths.
Convert to the newsprint or grayscale profile the paper specifies.
avoid: Fine hairlines and tiny reversed type.
Heavy total ink coverage that causes dot gain and show-through.
Building bleed into the file for standard ROP placements.
Assuming one column width applies across papers.
Using light tints below about 10% or fine screens.
tips: Resolution of 200-300dpi is typical; line art 600-1200dpi.
Ads bill on column-inches, so check depth rounding on the rate card.
Preprint inserts have their own specs; this entry covers ROP ads.
Full-page ads often still leave a margin from page edge.
Test grayscale conversion before sending color art.

confidence: Low-Medium. 2-1/16in SAU column and 1/8in gutter corroborated; the 2-6 column totals come from a secondary source and one NJ Advance rate card shows a narrower 6-col width (~10.75-10.87in). Example depths, page sizes, dpi and ink limit are typical, not sourced.

name: Trade Publication
summary: Trade magazines use similar CMYK PDF/X-1a specs to consumer titles, with many using a 7.875 x 10.5in or 8.375 x 10.875in trim.
rules: Supply a composite CMYK PDF with PDF/X-1a setting; embed all fonts and graphics.
Graphics at 300dpi minimum; no color separations.
Full-page and spread ads bleed 0.125in; fractional ads typically do not bleed.
Heat Treat Today asks 0.5in live-matter margin from trim on bleed ads; others use 0.25in.
Trim size differs by title; confirm with each publication's rate card.

do: Build to the exact publication spec sheet.
Keep logos and text 0.5in from trim on bleed ads for safety.
Use rich black sparingly and within ink limit.
Supply a proof if color matching matters.
Provide fractional ads at exact non-bleed sizes.
avoid: Mixing RGB and CMYK elements.
Sending layered or live-font files.
Placing text across the gutter.
Using trim size dimensions as bleed file size.
Assuming sizes are interchangeable between titles.
tips: Several trades share 7.875 x 10.5in trim; the bleed file is 8.125 x 10.75in.
Cover positions often have premium or extra specs.
Some publishers add a rule around undefined fractional ads.
Check digital and e-newsletter specs separately.
Ask about ad insertion order deadlines and material due dates.

name: Out-of-Home Print Poster
summary: Printed OOH posters and bulletins are produced to vendor-specified panel sizes, usually as large-format PDFs at reduced resolution.
rules: Specs are set by the OOH vendor (e.g. Lamar, Clear Channel Outdoor); confirm before building.
Common poster panels: 30-sheet (about 11 x 23ft overall) and 14 x 48ft bulletin; art area is smaller than panel.
Bleed and safe margins vary by vendor; the values here are placeholders - confirm.
Build at scale (e.g. 1/4 or 1/10 size) at higher effective dpi; confirm vendor rules.
Provide CMYK PDF with fonts outlined unless vendor instructs otherwise.

do: Use few words and large, high-contrast type.
Keep key content centered and away from edges.
Confirm panel size, bleed and scale with the vendor.
Include a logo and a single clear call to action.
Check legibility at distance.
avoid: Small body copy and dense layouts.
Thin fonts and low-contrast color pairs.
Placing critical content near panel edges.
Assuming the same file works across panel types.
Heavy text or QR codes too small to scan.
tips: Ask the vendor for a template per panel.
Effective dpi can be low for large-format viewing distance.
Most poster copy is read in seconds; aim for about 7 words.
Confirm illumination (backlit) needs for color.
Allow lead time for printing and shipping.

sizes.label: 30-Sheet Poster (art area approx.)
sizes.note: Approx. 22ft 5in x 10ft 2in art area as commonly cited; low confidence - confirm vendor spec.

sizes.label: Bulletin (14 x 48 ft)
sizes.note: 14ft x 48ft panel in inches; vendor may specify visible area. Confirm with vendor.

sizes.label: Mini-Poster / Bus Shelter (4ft x 6ft)
sizes.note: Common default 4 x 6ft; confirm with vendor.

sources: Not verified via fetched sources; general industry knowledge
confidence: Low. OOH panel dimensions, dpi and bleed are not backed by sources fetched in this research; treat as placeholders until checked against vendor spec sheets.
